The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with numerous small dark brown/black spots scattered across the surface, accompanied by significant yellow (chlorotic) areas. The spots are small and somewhat angular.

This is a leaf disease. Top candidates from the part index: Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Early_Blight, Leaf_Mold, Verticillium_Wilt, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus.

Let me view one reference from each of my top 8 candidates.

Bacterial Speck shows fewer, more discrete spots on a mostly green leaf. Septoria shows dense small dark spots on a heavily yellowed leaf, much closer to the test image. Let me continue with the remaining 6 candidates.
TSWV shows bronzing (purplish tint) rather than yellowing. Bacterial Canker shows marginal leaf scorch. Neither matches the test image well. Continuing with 4 more candidates.
Early Blight shows larger, more irregular dark lesions. Leaf Mold shows diffuse yellowing without distinct spots. Neither matches as well as Septoria. Two more to check.

Verticillium Wilt shows drooping/wilting without spots. Cucumber Mosaic shows stunted, curled leaves. Neither matches.

All 8 views used. Summary of comparison:

| Class | Match Quality | Key Difference |
|-------|--------------|----------------|
| **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch** | **Best** | Dense small dark spots on yellowed leaf matches perfectly |
| Bacterial_Speck | Partial | Spots similar but leaf stays green, fewer spots |
| Early_Blight | Partial | Lesions much larger |
| TSWV | Poor | Bronzing, not yellowing |
| Bacterial_Canker | Poor | Marginal scorch pattern |
| Leaf_Mold | Poor | Diffuse yellowing, no distinct spots |
| Verticillium_Wilt | Poor | Wilting, no spots |
| Cucumber_Mosaic | Poor | Stunting/curling, no spots |

The test image shows numerous **small** dark brown spots densely scattered across a leaf with extensive **yellow chlorosis**. This matches Septoria perfectly: small spots (< 1/8 inch), dark brown perimeter, yellow halo, multiplying to cause widespread leaf blight. The Septoria reference image was visually the closest match.
